Slots.maps_to: encounter/_slot_order (proposed shared mechanism id) -- decimillipede.py::DecimillipedeEncounter.create_monsters never sets Creature.slot_name
Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: DecimillipedeElite.cs:14 declares Slots=["segment1","segment2","segment3"], and GenerateMonsters (DecimillipedeElite.cs:43-48) tags each returned tuple with the matching slot string in order (Front->segment1, Middle->segment2, Back->segment3). `DecimillipedeEncounter.create_monsters` (decimillipede.py:163-202) never assigns `monster.slot_name`, and the `DecimillipedeEncounter` dataclass instance (`DECIMILLIPEDE_ELITE = DecimillipedeEncounter(id="decimillipede_elite")`) never sets `slots=` either, so `Encounter.get_next_slot`/`last_free_slot` have an empty row for this unit where the game has a real 3-entry one. EXECUTED WITNESS (enumeration, not argument): grepped every C# consumer of `Creature.SlotName` game-wide (`grep -rln SlotName src/`) -- 16 files total: the mechanism's own definition/sort sites (CombatManager.cs, CombatState.cs, ICombatState.cs, NullCombatState.cs, Creature.cs, EncounterModel.cs), five OTHER monsters' own move/spawn logic (Exoskeleton.cs, Myte.cs, Ovicopter.cs, PhantasmalGardener.cs, TwoTailedRat.cs, Wriggler.cs), two powers that spawn replacements into a vacated slot (InfestedPower.cs -- confirmed via `grep -rln InfestedPower src/Core/Models/Monsters/` to belong to PhrogParasite, an unrelated Overgrowth-act monster, not InfestedPrism -- and StockPower.cs), and one UI-only bestiary layout file (NBestiaryLayoutDecimillipede.cs). None of DecimillipedeSegment.cs, DecimillipedeSegmentFront.cs, DecimillipedeSegmentMiddle.cs, DecimillipedeSegmentBack.cs, or ReattachPower.cs read `SlotName`. Cross-checked the sim side too: `decimillipede.py` and `powers.py`'s `ReattachPower` never call `CreatureCmd.add`/re-seat a segment into a slot (a withered segment stays in `Enemies` and keeps its list position -- `ReattachPower.should_power_be_removed_after_owner_death` returns False, no removal ever happens). So today, for this specific unit, the missing Slots/slot_name modeling has no reader on either side -- confirmed dormant, not merely argued. It would go live the moment either side ports a slot-targeted mid-combat re-seat for a Decimillipede segment, or any cross-unit feature keys off `Creature.slot_name` expecting "segment1"/2/3. Separately: even if `SortEnemiesBySlotName` (CombatState.cs:495-501) fired today, it would be a no-op regardless, because `GenerateMonsters`' own return ORDER already equals the Slots row order (Front=segment1@0, Middle=segment2@1, Back=segment3@2) -- so the one thing that actually IS observable (enemy list order, hence targeting/indexing) already matches without any sort. Proposing shared mechanism id `encounter/_slot_order` for this family (also filed against kaiser_crab in this batch) since it recurs wherever an encounter declares Slots purely for a row that its own roster order already satisfies.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: DecimillipedeElite.cs:35-49: three segments (Front, Middle, Back, in that order) with `StarterMoveIdx` staggered by exactly one `base.Rng.NextInt(3)` draw (`num`), then `(num+1)%3` and `(num+2)%3` for Middle and Back -- one draw total. `decimillipede.py::DecimillipedeEncounter.create_monsters` (decimillipede.py:163-175) draws `start = selection_rng.next_int(3)` once (parity) and builds `[Front(starter=start), Middle(starter=(start+1)%3), Back(starter=(start+2)%3)]` -- identical order, identical modular stagger, identical single draw. The C#'s `AfterAddedToRoom` even-and-unique-HP pass (rounds MaxHp up to even, then +2 while a teammate already holds that value, wrapping MinInitialHp<->MaxInitialHp) is reproduced verbatim by the sim in TWO places -- `DecimillipedeSegment.adjust_hp_after_added` (the real hook-driven mirror, decimillipede.py:54-79) AND, redundantly but harmlessly, inline in `create_monsters` itself (decimillipede.py:176-201, explicitly documented as provably inert since parity mode's Niche roll overwrites it before the hook-driven pass ever reads a stale value). Roster, order, draw count and the HP-uniqueness side-effect all match.

guards.what: Out-of-kind note: withered-segment persistence (ReattachPower, "death does not mean removal") -- not an encounter-generation concern
guards.rationale: The batch brief named this unit's ReattachPower/withered-segment mechanic as calibration context. It is a monster/power-tier hook (`ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal`/`ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath` -> `powers.py::ReattachPower.should_owner_death_trigger_fatal`/`should_power_be_removed_after_owner_death`), never touched by `EncounterModel.GenerateMonsters` or any hook this record verdicts, so it is out of the `encounter` kind's surface. Spot-checked only: `powers.py:2933-2951` carries explicit C# line citations (`ReattachPower.cs:98-101`, `:106-109`) and matches the described behavior. Not filed as a finding here; belongs to the power/monster tier's own record if not already covered there (the monster stream's 2026-07-27 campaign audited all 109 monsters).
